context.hint: A local YAML scanner verifies a terminal ECDSA signature over template bytes. Verification previously removed every digest-prefixed line before hashing and selected the first digest, so a CR-terminated second digest line plus CR-separated code verified while the parser exposed the code. LF and CRLF tails failed. The current repair task is to define a terminal-signature boundary that leaves exactly one signature line outside the hashed bytes, rejects extra non-whitespace content after it, and still accepts valid LF, CRLF, trailing-newline and trailing-space signatures. Disposable local fixtures cover HTTP, code and DNS template shapes.
context.surface: Go command-line scanner with YAML template loading, HTTP, code and DNS request sections, and a local ECDSA signer/verifier. Disposable local templates, a locally generated certificate and private key, and a local template-parser harness; no network target is used.
assumptions: The attacker can edit a signed template file before the scanner loads it, but cannot forge an ECDSA signature or read the signer's private key.
The operator has enabled execution of code-template sections, so parsed code content is security-relevant.
The scanner loads local template files and the signer/verifier is reachable through a small local harness; no public service or deployed target is involved.
Signature lines follow the existing convention of one terminal digest-prefixed line appended after the template body.
Official benchmark verification is performed by an external host evaluator; local signing, parsing and regression checks are supporting evidence.

incumbent.text: Hypothesis: verification uses the first digest match for the signature while removing later digest-prefixed lines from the hashed bytes, so an extra digest line can be tolerated or can change which digest is trusted. Prerequisites: a valid signed template, ability to insert digest-prefixed lines, and a local verifier. Bounded test: append a malformed second digest line with LF and no code; separately prepend a malformed digest line before the real signature; compare verification errors. Expected supporting result: the later malformed digest is tolerated, while a first-position malformed digest is selected and fails. Falsifier: both arrangements fail, or the later malformed line changes the hash and fails. Cleanup: remove the disposable fixtures. Limitation: this tests digest selection, not the CR-tail execution path.

candidates.text: Hypothesis: a strict tail-boundary parser that splits raw bytes at the final digest-prefixed line and rejects any earlier digest line or non-whitespace suffix closes the CR-tail path. Prerequisites: repaired verifier, disposable LF/CRLF/CR fixtures and a local key. Bounded test: sign each fixture, append executable CR and LF tails, and run the repaired verifier. Expected supporting result: CR and LF tails fail while all untouched signed fixtures verify. Falsifier: a CR tail with code still verifies or a trailing-space valid signature fails. Cleanup: delete generated fixtures and keys. Limitation: the rule must also define how multiple digest-looking body lines are handled.

Hypothesis: verification should hash every byte except exactly one terminal signature block, rather than stripping all digest-looking lines anywhere; this removes both the multiple-signature and CR-tail discrepancies. Prerequisites: repaired verifier, a local ECDSA signer, and a parser harness. Bounded test: implement a final-non-whitespace-line helper that recognizes LF, CRLF and bare CR; use it for terminal digest selection and for removing only that one line; then run the CR/LF/CRLF matrix, body-tamper checks and representative signed templates. Expected supporting result: CR, LF and CRLF executable tails fail; valid LF and CRLF signatures and trailing whitespace pass. Falsifier: an executable tail still verifies or a valid signature regresses. Cleanup: restore the pristine source copy after recording the patch. Limitation: embedded digest-looking body lines become part of the signed range.

Hypothesis: the primary defect is normalization asymmetry between signer and verifier, so a body rewritten from LF to CR after signing can still verify while the parser sees modified content. Prerequisites: a signed LF template and a verifier with normalization logic. Bounded test: sign an LF body, rewrite interior line endings to CR while preserving the signature, and compare verification before and after repair. Expected supporting result: the rewritten body fails only after normalization is made symmetric. Falsifier: the rewritten body fails in both versions, or a legitimate Windows-style save also breaks. Cleanup: restore fixture copies. Limitation: may be a secondary effect rather than the execution path.

Hypothesis: trailing-byte tolerance around the digest line (spaces, tabs, double newlines, mixed endings) creates ambiguity that lets a mutated tail verify; the repair should accept one documented canonical suffix and reject non-canonical tails. Prerequisites: valid signed fixtures and a local verifier. Bounded test: generate signatures followed by newline, CRLF, space, tab and double-newline tails and compare acceptance before and after repair. Expected supporting result: exactly the documented benign forms remain accepted. Falsifier: a non-canonical tail is accepted while an equally benign documented form is rejected. Cleanup: delete generated variants. Limitation: canonical-form selection is a policy choice.

Hypothesis: repair closure requires representative benign templates across independent sections to verify and one-byte mutations in each section to fail, in LF and CRLF forms. Prerequisites: repaired verifier and disposable HTTP, code and DNS templates. Bounded test: sign each template, mutate one byte outside the signature, and compare verifier results in a single matrix. Expected supporting result: all untouched templates verify and all mutations fail. Falsifier: a mutation is accepted or an untouched template is rejected. Cleanup: reset the disposable source tree. Limitation: validation activity rather than a distinct root-cause repair.

evaluations.rationale: Selected. The existing matrix showed extra digest lines are tolerated and the CR tail is removed from the hashed range. Hashing every byte except one terminal signature block is a minimal rule that covers both observations and is directly testable on a fresh source copy.
Deferred, not refuted. Strict last-line parsing is the right direction, but the proposal did not unify terminal-signature selection, multiple digest lines and CRLF handling into one rule.
Incumbent. Its multiple-signature mechanism was confirmed, but it was a diagnostic hypothesis rather than the concrete terminal-signature repair.
Deferred. Representative-template regression closure was valuable and was incorporated into the selected repair test, but it is validation rather than a root-cause change.
Deferred, not refuted. The CRLF behavior observed in the matrix makes normalization asymmetry plausible, but it was less directly connected than the terminal boundary.
Deferred. Trailing spaces and newlines already verified before repair, so this candidate is regression coverage rather than an explanation of the executable bypass.

observation.summary: Implemented a terminal-signature boundary in a disposable copy: a helper locates the final non-whitespace line using LF, CRLF and bare CR; signature removal and digest lookup operate only on that line; verification reads the terminal digest. The patch applied cleanly to a fresh copy and produced byte-identical source. The repaired matrix rejected CR-tail, LF-tail and CRLF-tail executable variants while accepting valid LF, CRLF, trailing-newline and trailing-space signatures. A 20-check regression matrix over HTTP, code and DNS template shapes passed, including body tampering, embedded digest-looking comments and a stripped-bytes equality check. The real template parser on repaired source reported the CR-tail file as unverified while still parsing the appended code request; the pristine parser reported the same file as verified with the code request present. A cross-version check showed pristine-signed and repaired-signed ordinary templates verify under both implementations. The official host evaluator has not run.
observation.next_hint: The local repair closes the reproduced CR-tail and multiple-signature boundary for ordinary templates. Remaining limits are the missing official verdict, imported code-file signatures, zero-width-byte tails and exact parity with the pinned official image.
